title: 15 Everyday Phrasal Verbs
summary: Learn 15 common phrasal verbs that native speakers use every day. Boost your English speaking skills with simple examples.

sections.p: Phrasal verbs combine a verb and a small word like up or out. They change the meaning of the main verb completely. When you start your day, you need to leave your bed, stop sleeping, and put on your clothes. These everyday actions use simple phrasal verbs that you will hear all the time in friendly conversations.

ex.en: I usually get up at seven o'clock in the morning.
Please wake up, it is time for breakfast.
ex.mean: Stop sleeping and open your eyes

ex.en: Hurry up and put on your jacket!

sections.p: When you lose something around the house, you need to search for it until you locate it. Sometimes tasks are too difficult, and people want to stop trying. However, it is important to keep going and never quit! Learning these useful phrases will help you talk about everyday problems and success.

ex.en: I am looking for my keys in the living room.
Never give up when learning a new language.
ex.mean: Stop trying because something is hard

ex.en: Please turn off the lights before you leave.
ex.mean: Stop a machine or light from working

sections.p: We often use phrasal verbs when talking about our homes and social lives. You might need to take care of a pet, write down a phone number, or throw away old paper in the bin. These natural expressions make your English sound much more polite and native.

ex.en: Can you look after my cat this weekend?
ex.mean: Take care of someone or something

ex.en: Write down your new address on this paper.
Throw away that old box in the kitchen.

sections.p: Finally, let us look at verbs for social events and information. You might bump into an old friend at the supermarket by surprise, or fill out a form with your personal details. Knowing these final phrasal verbs completes your basic daily vocabulary.

ex.en: I ran into my teacher at the shop yesterday.
Please fill out this form with your name.
Turn on the TV to watch the news.

tip: Do not memorize them as isolated words. Learn each phrasal verb with a real sentence about your own daily routine.

quiz.en: I need to ___ my keys because I cannot find them anywhere.
Please ___ your warm coat because it is very cold outside.
Do not ___! You can learn English if you practice every day.
Can you ___ the lights when you leave the room?
I want to ___ my dog while I am at work.
Please ___ this information on a piece of paper.
